title: Singapore sets AI risk guidelines as insurers brace for agent claims
dek: Singapore finalised AI risk guidelines for financial firms, insurers are bracing for claims from rogue agents, JPMorgan's Jamie Dimon says AI threats went up 10-fold after Mythos, and HSBC plans deep AI-linked job cuts.

body.head: Singapore sets the guidelines
body.text: MAS, Singapore's financial regulator, has issued its finalised Guidelines on AI Risk Management. MAS expects financial institutions to maintain inventories of their AI use and apply controls in areas including data governance, cybersecurity, testing and human oversight. The guidelines phase in, with sections 3 and 4 taking effect on 7 October 2027, and MAS intends to consult the sector in 2027 on what additional guidance for agentic AI would be useful.
support: The Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) has issued its finalised Guidelines on AI Risk Management for financial institutions.

MAS expects financial institutions to maintain inventories of their AI use and apply controls covering areas such as data governance, cybersecurity, testing, human oversight, monitoring and change management.
Implementation will take place in phases. Sections 3 and 4 will take effect on 7 October 2027, while Sections 5 and 6 will apply from 7 October 2028.
In 2027, the regulator intends to consult the financial sector on what additional guidance for agentic AI would be useful.

body.head: Insurers brace for agent claims
body.text: Insurers are bracing for claims worth millions from AI agents that have spun out of control, and Tim Rayner, head of underwriting and claims at Verisk, says the buck stops with the CEO. The Financial Times reports that the personal liability of executives such as OpenAI's Sam Altman and Anthropic's Dario Amodei is now in play too.
support: Insurers are bracing for claims worth millions from AI agents that have spun out of control.
The Financial Times reports that the personal liability of executives like Sam Altman (OpenAI) and Dario Amodei (Anthropic) is now in play, too.

Incidents like the hack of AI platform Hugging Face by OpenAI agents are driving the shift. Tim Rayner, head of underwriting and claims at Verisk, says the buck stops with the CEO. Every company leader must ensure proper oversight, and AI doesn't change that. If OpenAI carries directors and officers (D&O) insurance, it could cover costs from lawsuits against Altman.

body.head: Dimon sees a 10-fold jump
body.text: JPMorgan CEO Jamie Dimon said threats related to AI "went up 10-fold after Mythos," Anthropic's model. Anthropic, for its part, now reserves the top tier of its Cyber Verification Program, Specialized Access, for verified organizations authorized to test systems such as interbank transfer infrastructure, and partners in its earlier Project Glasswing program uncovered at least 129,000 verified software vulnerabilities between April and July 2026.
support: JPMorgan CEO Jamie Dimon says cybersecurity risks soared when Anthropic released its Mythos AI model.
Threats related to artificial intelligence (AI) “went up 10-fold after Mythos,” Dimon said in an interview Tuesday (Oct. 6) with Bloomberg TV.

We’re launching a new, expanded version of our Cyber Verification Program (CVP), which makes advanced cyber capabilities and reduced blocking classifiers available to qualifying security professionals.

Specialized Access , which has the fewest cyber blocks, is reserved for a limited set of verified organizations that are authorized to test safety systems that could impact people’s lives or disrupt markets, such as flight operating systems, power grids, telecom networks, interbank transfer infrastructure, and government administrative networks.
Through the program, our partners uncovered at least 129,000 verified software vulnerabilities between April and July 2026.
Partners in the predecessor program, Project Glasswing , found at least 129,000 confirmed vulnerabilities between April and July 2026, according to Anthropic.

body.head: HSBC plans deep cuts
body.text: HSBC is planning job cuts across its UK wealth management business as part of a broader push to integrate artificial intelligence, the Financial Times reported, and reductions among financial advisers could reach around 70 per cent. The bank plans to cut about half of management and specialist roles in the business, the report said.
support: HSBC is planning sweeping job cuts across its UK wealth management business, including a sharp reduction in financial advisers and specialist staff, as part of a broader push to integrate artificial intelligence, the Financial Times reported on Wednesday (Oct 7).

The bank plans to cut about half of management and specialist roles in the business, while reductions among financial advisers could reach around 70 per cent, the report said, citing people familiar with the plans.

body.head: Start with the inventory
body.text: MAS expects financial institutions to maintain inventories of their AI use. A useful one lists each model and agent, who owns it and what it can reach, and gives a regulator, an insurer and a security team one place to start.
support: MAS expects financial institutions to maintain inventories of their AI use and apply controls covering areas such as data governance, cybersecurity, testing, human oversight, monitoring and change management.

suggestion: A line on how your own clients are starting their AI inventories, or what they find hardest to list, would fit at the end of the last section.
